Find the leak without opening the wall.

Acoustic and thermal imaging to pinpoint hidden leaks without demolition. Move the lens below to see how a hidden leak shows up.

Scanning. Move the lens over the wall.

The tools we use, and what each one is good at

Acoustic listening

How it works
Sensitive microphones pick up the sound of water escaping a pressurized pipe. We follow it to the loudest point.
Best for
Supply lines inside walls, under slabs and buried in the yard.
Keep in mind
Very small leaks and noisy surroundings can hide the sound, so we back it up with another tool.

Where hidden leaks usually are

  • Under the slab

    Hot and cold lines buried in concrete.

  • Inside walls

    Supply lines behind drywall and tile.

  • Above ceilings

    Bathroom and kitchen lines overhead.

  • Under sinks and fixtures

    Slow drips at valves and supply hoses.

  • Around the water heater

    Fittings and connections that wear over time.

  • Yard and irrigation

    Buried service and sprinkler lines.

Check your meter in 30 minutes

  1. 1Turn off every tap and appliance that uses water.
  2. 2Find your water meter and its small leak indicator (a dial or triangle).
  3. 3If it's moving, or the reading changes after 30 minutes, water is going somewhere.
  4. 4Call us before the damage spreads.

Other signs to watch for

  • A water bill that climbs with no change in use
  • The sound of running water when everything is off
  • Warm spots on the floor, which can mean a hot water line under the slab
  • A musty smell or visible mold
  • Stains, bubbling paint or warped flooring
  • Lower water pressure than usual

Think there's a leak you can't see?

We scan first and open as little as possible, so repairs stay small and your walls and floors stay intact.
